name: TibaCheck — Site Audit
author: omwamij

sections.description:
Is your WordPress site quietly exposed? TibaCheck answers that in one click — a read-only security and health audit that checks the places hacked sites hide, in plain language anyone can act on.

Run the audit and you get two scores — a Site Health Score and a Security Score — followed by every finding marked Pass, Warn, or Fail, each with what it means and why it matters. No settings are changed, nothing phones home, and the audit runs entirely on your own site.

What makes TibaCheck different:

  • It hunts persistence, not just problems — hidden administrator accounts, must-use plugins and drop-ins, database triggers, mystery cron jobs, and stray code files: the survival tricks malware uses to come back after a cleanup.
  • 52 read-only checks across updates, accounts, exposure, settings, and comments — plus a 5-check WooCommerce store pack that appears automatically on shops.
  • A Plugins Review in every report — every installed plugin grouped by the job it does, with overlaps flagged.
  • The Watch — the same audit re-runs weekly on WordPress’s own scheduler and flags anything that gets worse. No external calls, ever.
  • A printable client report — built for site owners, freelancers, and care-plan teams who report to clients.

TibaCheck runs a read-only audit of your site’s configuration and shows you, in plain language, what needs attention. Every report leads with two scores — a Site Health Score and a Security Score built from checks mapped to the OWASP Top 10 (2025) — with a full OWASP coverage table showing what was assessed and what needs an external deep scan.

The 52 read-only checks cover:

  • Updates & platform — pending core, plugin and theme updates; the automatic-update switches; PHP version and critical PHP security advisories; missing PHP extensions; backup status; site email delivery; administration email; privacy policy page
  • Accounts & access — user accounts, including administrators hidden from WordPress’s own lists; registration safety; application passwords; login keys and salts; privilege audit; XML-RPC access; the file editor
  • Exposure & persistence — debug display; exposed debug and PHP error logs; exposed PHP configuration and backup files; stray code in wp-content, the site root and uploads; server config in uploads; must-use plugins and drop-ins; database triggers; cron job origins; server prepend directives; file permissions; inactive plugins and themes; active plugin files; active theme
  • Settings & comments — search visibility; SSL / HTTPS; permalinks; site timezone; homepage and posts-page display; avatar rating; autoload size; cron health; comments on new posts; comment queues, approval, name and email, comments on old posts, comment notifications, and pingbacks & trackbacks; update services
  • WooCommerce store pack — store pages, payment gateways, store details, checkout posture and store visibility for shops

Every report also includes a Plugins Review — every installed plugin grouped by the job it does — and a printable client report. The Watch re-runs the same audit weekly on WordPress’s built-in scheduler, with no external calls, and flags anything that gets worse.

TibaCheck never changes your site’s content or settings — it reports; fixing is up to you, or the care-plan team that handles it every month. It does not claim to scan for malware by signature: it audits the places malware must live, persist and act — its hiding spots, its survival tricks, and the accounts it needs — and names what it finds.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/tibacheck-site-audit, or install through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Tools → Site Audit and click Run Audit.
sections.faq:
Does the audit change anything on my site?

No. Every check is read-only — TibaCheck never updates, deletes, or modifies your site. It stores only its own last report (scores and check statuses), any pending Watch change alert, and the time of the last automatic Watch run, so it can show your trend on the next run.

Does TibaCheck phone home or collect my data?

No. The audit makes no external requests at all — everything runs on your own server, and nothing about your site is sent anywhere. The weekly Watch uses WordPress’s built-in scheduler, not an outside service.

Will it slow my site down?

The audit runs only when you click Run Audit, plus one scheduled run a week. Between runs the plugin does nothing on your pages.

How is this different from a malware scanner?

Signature scanners look for known malware patterns inside files — and modern, per-site malware is built to miss signatures, from inside the same environment it hides from. TibaCheck instead audits the places malware must live, persist, and act: hidden accounts, drop-ins, triggers, cron jobs, and stray code. It names what it finds; it does not claim to certify a site clean.

What does the WooCommerce store pack check?

On sites running WooCommerce, five more checks appear automatically: store pages, payment gateways, store details, checkout posture, and store visibility — the failures that silently stop a shop from selling.

Is the OWASP score a certification?

No. The Security check score maps this plugin’s checks to the OWASP Top 10 (2025) categories they assess, and the coverage table labels every mapped category as partial. A passing check does not establish category-wide security. Injection, insecure design and logging/alerting remain unassessed. The score is a TibaCheck heuristic, not an OWASP certification, and is withheld when mapped evidence is incomplete. Separate code, architecture or dynamic assessment is required.

What do the statuses mean?

Pass — healthy. Warn — should be fixed soon. Fail — fix now; this is how sites get hacked or break.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. TibaCheck Pro adds deep file-integrity scanning (core checksum verification and file-content inspection), vulnerability monitoring, and scheduled scans. The free audit is complete on its own — Pro is for owners and care teams who need the deeper layer.
